title: Teken- en Ontwerpmodule
ai_prompts:
## Teken- en Ontwerpmodule

**Summary:** The Teken- en Ontwerpmodule feature allows users to create and design their own spaces, enabling them to visualize and plan their projects more effectively.

**User story:** As a user, I want to be able to create and design my own spaces using a drawing and design module, so that I can visualize and plan my projects more effectively.

**Problem / context:** Currently, users lack a dedicated tool for creating and designing their own spaces, making it difficult for them to visualize and plan their projects. This feature aims to fill this gap and provide users with a more immersive and interactive experience.

**Scope**
- In scope: Developing a drawing and design module that allows users to create and customize their own spaces, including adding walls, doors, windows, and other elements.
- Out of scope (non-goals): 
  - Integration with external design software
  - Advanced 3D modeling capabilities
  - Collaboration features for multiple users

**User flow**
Step 1: User accesses the Teken- en Ontwerpmodule feature from the main menu.
Step 2: User is presented with a blank canvas and a toolbar with various design elements (walls, doors, windows, etc.).
Step 3: User selects and adds design elements to the canvas, customizing their space as desired.
Step 4: User can save and load their designs, as well as export them as images or other file formats.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The user can access the Teken- en Ontwerpmodule feature from the main menu.
- [ ] The user is presented with a blank canvas and a toolbar with design elements.
- [ ] The user can add and customize design elements on the canvas.
- [ ] The user can save and load their designs.
- [ ] The user can export their designs as images or other file formats.

**Edge cases & error handling**
- Handling cases where the user attempts to add too many design elements, causing performance issues.
- Handling cases where the user attempts to save or export a design with invalid or corrupted data.

**Technical notes**
- Likely affected files/modules: The feature will likely involve updates to the existing UI components, as well as the addition of new modules for handling design data and exporting files.
- Data model / API changes: The feature will require changes to the data model to store design data, as well as API updates to handle saving and loading designs.
- Dependencies or integration points: The feature will likely depend on existing libraries for handling graphics and file exports.
- Non-functional constraints (perf, security, rate limits, etc.): The feature should be optimized for performance, ensuring that it can handle complex designs without significant lag or slowdown.

**Assumptions**
- The feature will follow existing convention in terms of UI design and layout.
- The feature will use existing libraries and frameworks for handling graphics and file exports.
- The feature will be built using the same technology stack as the rest of the application.

**Open questions**
- How will the feature handle cases where the user attempts to add design elements that are not compatible with each other (e.g. adding a door to a wall that is not thick enough to support it)?

**Definition of done**
- The feature is fully implemented and functional, with all acceptance criteria met.
- The feature has been thoroughly tested for edge cases and error handling.
- The feature has been reviewed and approved by the design and product teams.

title: Grid-gebaseerd 2D Canvas
description:
Als gebruiker wil ik een infinite werkveld met een "snap-to-grid" functie (bijv. per 50mm of 100mm)  zodat muren snel recht getekend kunnen worden, zoals te zien is op de wireframe. Deze snap functie kan aan of uitgetoggled worden aangezien dit soms belemmerend kan zijn voor de gebruiker

Als gebruiker kan ik op de muur drawing tool (pencil icon) klikken zodanig dat ik door punten op het werkveld te zetten automatisch muren worden getekend.

Alle muren worden by default op 90° hoeken getekend wanneer dit niet het geval is wordt automatisch de angle tussen de muren getoond. 

![afbeelding](https://wqsnmavcmycznzzdjxwj.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/item-images/img_mu5czj7i_p61t8k.png)
Iedere muur kan door de gebruiker steeds worden aangepast door de ankor punten of de gehele muur te verslepen. Daarnaast wordt op elk muur ook steeds een aanduiding gegeven van de effectieve afmetingen in een pill zodanig dat de gebruiker steeds de nauwkeurige afmetingen kan zien van de muur in kwestie.

<!--attachments-start-->
- [geplakte-afbeelding.png](https://wqsnmavcmycznzzdjxwj.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/item-images/img_mu5czj7i_p61t8k.png)
<!--attachments-end-->
ai_prompts:
## Grid-gebaseerd 2D Canvas

**Summary:** Implement a grid-based 2D canvas with snap-to-grid functionality to enable users to quickly draw walls at right angles.

**User story:** As a user, I want to draw walls on a grid-based 2D canvas with a snap-to-grid function, so that I can efficiently create floor plans with accurate measurements.

**Problem / context:** Currently, users may struggle to draw walls at precise angles, leading to inaccurate floor plans and frustrating user experience.

**Scope**
- In scope: Implementing the grid-based 2D canvas, snap-to-grid functionality, wall drawing tool, and anchor points for wall adjustment.
- Out of scope (non-goals): 
  - Implementing a 3D visualization of the floor plan.
  - Allowing users to import or export floor plans from/to other software.
  - Creating a library of pre-designed floor plans or templates.

**User flow**
1. The user enters the 2D canvas view.
2. The user toggles the snap-to-grid function on or off.
3. The user clicks the wall drawing tool (pencil icon) and starts drawing walls by setting points on the grid.
4. The system automatically draws walls at 90° angles and displays the angle between walls if not a right angle.
5. The user can adjust walls by dragging anchor points or the entire wall.
6. The system displays the effective dimensions of each wall in a pill, allowing users to see precise measurements.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The grid-based 2D canvas is displayed with a default grid size (e.g., 50mm or 100mm).
- [ ] The snap-to-grid function can be toggled on and off.
- [ ] Walls are automatically drawn at 90° angles when the snap-to-grid function is enabled.
- [ ] The angle between walls is displayed when not a right angle.
- [ ] Users can adjust walls by dragging anchor points or the entire wall.
- [ ] The effective dimensions of each wall are displayed in a pill.

**Edge cases & error handling**
- If the user attempts to draw a wall with an invalid angle, the system should display an error message or prevent the action.
- If the user tries to adjust a wall beyond the grid boundaries, the system should either prevent the action or adjust the wall to the nearest grid point.

**Technical notes**
- Likely affected files/modules: 2D canvas rendering, wall drawing tool, grid management, and dimension calculation.
- Data model / API changes: The system will need to store the grid size, wall coordinates, and dimensions.
- Dependencies or integration points: The 2D canvas library, grid management library, and dimension calculation library.
- Non-functional constraints (perf, security, rate limits, etc.): The system should render the grid and walls efficiently, even with complex floor plans.

**Assumptions**
- The default grid size will be 50mm, but this can be adjusted by the user.
- The wall drawing tool will be represented by a pencil icon.
- The system will use a standard 2D canvas library for rendering.
- The dimension calculation will be based on the grid size and wall coordinates.

**Open questions**
- How will the system handle cases where the user tries to draw a wall with an angle that is not a multiple of the grid size?
- Will the system allow users to customize the grid size, and if so, how will this be implemented?
- How will the system handle cases where the user tries to adjust a wall that is connected to other walls or objects?

**Definition of done**
- The grid-based 2D canvas is fully implemented and functional.
- The snap-to-grid function is working as expected.
- The wall drawing tool is implemented and allows users to draw walls at precise angles.
- The system displays the effective dimensions of each wall in a pill.
- All acceptance criteria are met, and the system passes all tests.

title: Deuren en ramen toevoegen
description:
Als gebruiker wil ik in staat zijn om deuren en ramen toe te voegen in het getekende grond plan. Op deze manier kan de gebruiker een nauwkeurigere weergave maken van het effectieve grondplan. 

Wanneer ik als gebruiker klik op de deur of raam tool, veranderd mijn cursor in een pen-nip icon. Hierdoor ziet de gebruiker dat hij nu iets kan plaatsen op de muur. Hierbij klikt de gebruiker op de plaats op de muur waar hij/zij het raam of deur wilt toevoegen. Eens geklikt krijgt de gebruiker een pop-up/slide-out waarin de gebruiker de breedte, hoogte en borstwering (afstand van vloer tot onderkant raam - enkel voor de raam tool) geeft en de gebruiker de nodige afmetingen kan invullen.

![afbeelding](https://wqsnmavcmycznzzdjxwj.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/item-images/img_mu5czr43_bn7tml.png)

<!--attachments-start-->
- [geplakte-afbeelding.png](https://wqsnmavcmycznzzdjxwj.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/item-images/img_mu5czr43_bn7tml.png)
<!--attachments-end-->
ai_prompts:
## Deuren en ramen toevoegen

**Summary:** Add doors and windows to the drawn floor plan to create a more accurate representation.

**User story:** As a user, I want to add doors and windows to the floor plan, so that I can create a more accurate and detailed representation of the space.

**Problem / context:** Currently, users cannot add doors and windows to the floor plan, which limits the accuracy and usefulness of the tool. This feature is needed to provide a more comprehensive and realistic representation of the space.

**Scope**
- In scope: Adding doors and windows to the floor plan, including specifying dimensions and placement.
- Out of scope (non-goals): 
  - Editing or deleting existing doors and windows (this will be handled in a separate feature).
  - Automatically generating door and window placements based on room type or other factors.
  - Integrating with external databases or APIs for door and window data.

**User flow**
1. The user clicks on the door or window tool, and the cursor changes to a pen-nib icon.
2. The user clicks on the wall where they want to add the door or window.
3. A pop-up or slide-out appears, allowing the user to enter the width, height, and (for windows) sill height (distance from floor to bottom of window).
4. The user enters the necessary dimensions and submits the form.
5. The door or window is added to the floor plan at the specified location and with the specified dimensions.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The cursor changes to a pen-nib icon when the door or window tool is selected.
- [ ] Clicking on the wall with the door or window tool opens a pop-up or slide-out for entering dimensions.
- [ ] The pop-up or slide-out includes fields for width, height, and (for windows) sill height.
- [ ] The user can enter valid dimensions and submit the form.
- [ ] The door or window is added to the floor plan at the specified location and with the specified dimensions.
- [ ] The door or window is displayed with the correct dimensions and orientation.

**Edge cases & error handling**
- If the user enters invalid dimensions (e.g. negative numbers), an error message is displayed and the door or window is not added.
- If the user attempts to add a door or window to a wall that is not valid (e.g. a wall that is too short), an error message is displayed and the door or window is not added.

**Technical notes**
- Likely affected files/modules: `floorPlan.js`, `tools.js`, `doorWindow.js`.
- Data model / API changes: The `FloorPlan` object will need to be updated to include doors and windows, with properties for location, dimensions, and type (door or window).
- Dependencies or integration points: The `Grid-gebaseerd 2D Canvas` feature will need to be integrated to display the doors and windows.
- Non-functional constraints (perf, security, rate limits, etc.): The feature should not significantly impact performance or security.

**Assumptions**
- The door and window tools will be added to the existing toolbar.
- The pop-up or slide-out for entering dimensions will follow the existing design pattern for forms and input fields.
- The doors and windows will be displayed using the existing rendering engine.

**Open questions**
- How will the doors and windows be snapped to the grid, if at all?
- Will there be any validation or restrictions on the dimensions that can be entered?
- How will the doors and windows be stored in the data model, and how will they be serialized and deserialized?

**Definition of done**
- The feature is fully implemented and tested.
- The acceptance criteria are met.
- The code is reviewed and approved by a peer.
- The feature is deployed to production and verified to be working as expected.

title: Split Room (Zone Tool)
description:
Essentieel voor de aangegeven hoogteverschillen. Met deze tool kan de gebruiker virtuele stippellijnen trekken om een ruimte in zones te verdelen. Per zone kan een andere plafondhoogte (bijv. h:2.2m en h:2.5m) gedefinieerd worden.

Wanneer een ruimte gesplit is zal in elke deel van deze ruimte een aparte hoogte pill getoond worden die de gebruiker weer kan aanpassen wanneer nodig.

![afbeelding](https://wqsnmavcmycznzzdjxwj.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/item-images/img_mu5czyq7_b2uw2m.png)

<!--attachments-start-->

<!--attachments-end-->
ai_prompts:
## Split Room (Zone Tool)

**Summary:** The Split Room feature allows users to divide a room into zones with different ceiling heights by drawing virtual dashed lines.

**User story:** As a user, I want to split a room into zones with different ceiling heights, so that I can accurately define and adjust the height of each zone.

**Problem / context:** Currently, users cannot define different ceiling heights within a single room, which can lead to inaccuracies in room design and planning. This feature is essential for handling height differences and providing a more realistic representation of the room.

**Scope**
- In scope: Creating a tool to draw virtual dashed lines to split a room into zones, assigning different ceiling heights to each zone, and displaying separate height pills for each zone.
- Out of scope (non-goals): Automatically generating zones based on room dimensions, integrating with external design software, or creating a 3D visualization of the room.

**User flow**
Step 1: User selects the Split Room tool and clicks on the room to start drawing a virtual dashed line.
Step 2: User draws the dashed line to split the room into zones.
Step 3: User assigns a ceiling height to each zone by interacting with the height pill.
Step 4: System updates the room display to show separate height pills for each zone.
Step 5: User can adjust the ceiling height of each zone by interacting with the corresponding height pill.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The user can draw virtual dashed lines to split a room into zones.
- [ ] Each zone can be assigned a different ceiling height.
- [ ] Separate height pills are displayed for each zone.
- [ ] The user can adjust the ceiling height of each zone by interacting with the corresponding height pill.
- [ ] The system updates the room display in real-time as the user adjusts the zone boundaries and ceiling heights.

**Edge cases & error handling**
- If the user attempts to draw a zone with invalid boundaries (e.g., intersecting lines), the system should prevent the action and display an error message.
- If the user assigns an invalid ceiling height (e.g., negative value), the system should prevent the action and display an error message.

**Technical notes**
- Likely affected files/modules: Room editor, Zone tool, Height pill component.
- Data model / API changes: The room data model will need to be updated to store zone boundaries and ceiling heights.
- Dependencies or integration points: The Zone tool will depend on the Room editor and Height pill component.
- Non-functional constraints (perf, security, rate limits, etc.): The system should be able to handle a large number of zones and ceiling height adjustments without significant performance degradation.

**Assumptions**
- The user will have a basic understanding of room design and planning concepts.
- The system will use a standard unit of measurement (e.g., meters) for ceiling heights.
- The Zone tool will follow existing convention in the Room editor for drawing and editing shapes.

**Open questions**
- How will the system handle cases where the user attempts to merge or delete zones?
- Will the system provide any snapping or alignment features to help users draw zone boundaries?
- How will the system display zone boundaries and ceiling heights when the room is zoomed out or in?

**Definition of done**
- The Split Room feature is fully implemented and functional.
- All acceptance criteria are met.
- The system handles edge cases and error scenarios correctly.
- The feature is thoroughly tested and validated by the QA team.

title: Hoogte definitie van ruimte
description: Wanneer ik als gebruiker een effectieve ruimte heb aangemaakt verschijnt in het centrum van de ruimte een pill waarin de hoogte van deze ruimte wordt weergeven. By default staat deze op 2,5m echter kan de gebrruiker deze waardes aanpassen door op deze pill te klikken. Dan krijgt de gebruiker een pop-up waarin hij/zij deze values kan aanpassen. (dit dient ook het geval te zijn voor alle muren --> On click op pill pop-up tonen waardoor de gebruiker de effectieve values kan aanpassen.
ai_prompts:
## Hoogte Definitie van Ruimte

**Summary:** Display and allow users to edit the height of a room through a pill in the room's center, with a default value of 2.5m.

**User story:** As a user, I want to easily view and edit the height of a room, so that I can accurately design and plan my space.

**Problem / context:** Currently, users lack a straightforward way to define and adjust the height of rooms in the Offerte builder, which can lead to inaccuracies in design and planning.

**Scope**
- In scope: Displaying the room height in a pill, allowing users to edit this value through a popup, and applying this functionality to all walls.
- Out of scope (non-goals): Automatically calculating room heights based on other factors, integrating this feature with the Gyproc calculator, or adding 3D visualization of room heights.

**User flow**
1. User creates a room in the Offerte builder.
2. A pill appears in the center of the room displaying the default height of 2.5m.
3. User clicks on the pill to edit the height.
4. A popup appears allowing the user to input a new height value.
5. User saves the new height value.
6. The pill updates to display the new height value.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The room height pill is displayed in the center of the room with a default value of 2.5m.
- [ ] Clicking on the room height pill opens a popup for editing the height value.
- [ ] The popup allows users to input and save a new height value.
- [ ] The room height pill updates to display the new height value after saving.
- [ ] This functionality is also applicable to all walls, allowing users to edit their heights through a similar pill and popup interface.

**Edge cases & error handling**
- If a user enters a non-numeric value, the popup should display an error message and prevent saving.
- If a user attempts to save a height value outside a reasonable range (e.g., less than 0 or greater than 10m), the popup should display a warning or error message.

**Technical notes**
- Likely affected files/modules: Room creation and editing modules, UI components for the room height pill and popup.
- Data model / API changes: Update the room data model to include a height attribute, and modify the API to accept and return this attribute.
- Dependencies or integration points: Follow existing convention in the Offerte builder for UI components and data models.
- Non-functional constraints (perf, security, rate limits, etc.): Ensure the popup and pill do not significantly impact page load times or responsiveness.

**Assumptions**
- The default height value of 2.5m is a sensible default for most use cases.
- The popup for editing the height value will follow the existing design patterns and conventions of the Offerte builder.
- The height values will be stored and retrieved in the same unit (e.g., meters) throughout the application.

**Open questions**
- How should the application handle cases where a user attempts to set a height value that is not a positive number?

**Definition of done**
- The feature is fully implemented and tested according to the acceptance criteria.
- The code is reviewed and merged into the main branch.
- Documentation is updated to reflect the new feature and its usage.

title: Summary widget
description:
Als gebruiker wil ik bovenaan de builder een summary widget krijg waarin ik een snel overzicht heb van de volgende values berekend op basis van het plan dat de gebruiker heeft getekend:
- Vloer oppervlak
- Muur oppervlak
- Plafond oppervlak

Hiervoor dienen dan ook de nodige calculatie methodes opgezet te worden om dit automatisch te berekenen op basis van de ingegeven grondplannen.
ai_prompts:
## Summary Widget

**Summary:** The summary widget displays a quick overview of calculated values (floor, wall, and ceiling surface areas) based on the user's drawn plan, providing a convenient summary of the project's dimensions.

**User story:** As a user, I want a summary widget at the top of the builder that shows the calculated surface areas of the floor, walls, and ceiling, so that I can easily review and verify my project's dimensions.

**Problem / context:** Currently, users lack a centralized and automated way to view the calculated surface areas of their project, making it difficult to quickly review and verify their design. This feature aims to address this issue by providing a concise summary of the project's dimensions.

**Scope**
- In scope: Developing a summary widget that displays calculated surface areas (floor, wall, and ceiling) based on the user's drawn plan.
- Out of scope (non-goals): 
  - Editing or modifying the plan directly from the summary widget.
  - Including additional calculated values beyond surface areas (e.g., volume, material quantities).
  - Providing detailed calculation methods or formulas within the widget.

**User flow**
Step 1: The user opens the builder and starts drawing their plan.
Step 2: As the user adds elements to their plan (walls, floors, ceilings), the summary widget updates in real-time to reflect the calculated surface areas.
Step 3: The user can view the summary widget at the top of the builder, which displays the calculated surface areas for the floor, walls, and ceiling.
Step 4: If the user makes changes to their plan, the summary widget updates automatically to reflect the new calculated values.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] The summary widget is displayed at the top of the builder.
- [ ] The widget shows the calculated surface areas for the floor, walls, and ceiling.
- [ ] The calculated values update in real-time as the user modifies their plan.
- [ ] The widget displays a loading state while calculations are being performed.
- [ ] The widget displays an error message if calculation fails.

**Edge cases & error handling**
- If the user's plan is empty or incomplete, the summary widget should display a message indicating that no calculations can be performed.
- If the calculation fails due to invalid user input or technical issues, the widget should display an error message.

**Technical notes**
- Likely affected files/modules: `SummaryWidget.js`, `Calculator.js`, `Plan.js`.
- Data model / API changes: The `Plan` model will need to be updated to include calculated surface areas.
- Dependencies or integration points: The summary widget will rely on the `Calculator` module to perform calculations.
- Non-functional constraints (perf, security, rate limits, etc.): The widget should update in real-time without causing significant performance issues.

**Assumptions**
- The calculation methods for surface areas will be implemented using existing geometric algorithms.
- The summary widget will follow the existing design patterns and styling conventions of the builder.

**Open questions**
- How should the widget handle cases where the user's plan is extremely large or complex, potentially causing performance issues?

**Definition of done**
- The summary widget is fully implemented and functional.
- The widget updates in real-time as the user modifies their plan.
- The calculated surface areas are accurate and consistent with the user's drawn plan.
- The widget handles edge cases and errors correctly.
- The code is reviewed, tested, and merged into the main branch.
feature_description: Je ziet nu direct in een overzicht bovenin je scherm wat het totale vloer-, muur- en plafondoppervlak van je ontwerp is. Deze waarden worden automatisch berekend terwijl je tekent, zodat je altijd een actueel inzicht hebt in de omvang van je project. Hierdoor bespaar je tijd en heb je direct de juiste cijfers bij de hand voor je calculaties.
estimated_tokens_reasoning: Dit vereist zowel de implementatie van geometrische berekeningslogica als het toevoegen van een nieuwe UI-component aan de builder-omgeving.
